summary.headline: D.P. Abhushan Q1 FY27 revenue rose 58% YoY to INR853.6 crore and PAT rose 77% to INR64 crore, but volume growth was only about 1-2%.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 58% YoY to INR853.63 crore, with EBITDA up 70% to INR93.99 crore and margin up 80 bps to 11.01%. PAT rose 77% to INR64 crore (7.55% margin). Management attributed most of the growth to higher gold prices and making charges rather than volume, with volume growth of about 1-2%. Expansion was briefly moderated in May after the gold import duty hike, and management says it has now returned to an aggressive expansion mode with a target of about 10% volume growth for FY27 and FY28.

financial_highlights.change: +58% YoY vs INR541 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Gold
segments.commentary: Revenue INR781 crore, up 59% YoY; management said only 10-15% of growth came from inventory gains and most of the rest from higher making charges.

segments.name: Silver
segments.commentary: Revenue INR40 crore, up 150% YoY from INR16 crore, described as a fast-growing category.

segments.name: Diamond / studded
segments.commentary: Revenue INR29 crore vs INR31 crore a year ago (down about 6%). Studded mix is 6-7% of sales; target 12-15% by March 2028, with diamond business targeted at 2x-3x current levels.

segments.name: Product category mix
segments.commentary: Wedding-related purchases 62% of sales, festive and lightweight 18%, and gifts/other 20%.

guidance_outlook: Volume growth target of approximately 10% for both FY27 and FY28 (internal planning target).
Store network target of 51 stores by FY30 (vs about 12 currently), with roughly 5-6 new stores planned in FY27 and 6-8 per year thereafter.
Internal store mix target: about 5-7 COCO-to-FOCO split indicated as 6-7 COCO and 1-2 FOCO in one answer, while another answer said 5-7 FOCO; the mix was not clearly consistent.
Studded share targeted to reach 12-15% of overall sales by March 2028.
Management expects gradual volume improvement in FY27 as gold prices settle, and festive sales from August to be disclosed.
capex_capacity: New showrooms finalised at Jabalpur (Madhya Pradesh, about 3,750 sq ft, first FOCO store, franchisee-owned company-operated) and Dahod (Gujarat, about 3,200 sq ft, COCO, entry into Gujarat); fit-out underway and openings expected soon.
Two new locations already finalised, two more under planning, and 2-3 more expected to be finalised by end of July 2026.

Store formats: small-to-medium at 3,000-5,000 sq ft and large at 8,000-10,000 sq ft; management cited breakeven in 6-9 months and mature turnover of INR150-200 crore (small) and INR350-400 crore (large) after 3-4 years.
Inventory turns: stores reach 3x inventory turnover in 2-3 years and 4.5-5x after 4-5 years. Company-wide inventory turnover is about 4.7x-5.0x annually.
demand_pricing: Footfall-to-conversion ratio of 81%; average ticket size about INR157,000.
Old gold exchange contributed about 25% of Q1 FY27 sales.
D.P. Swarna Plus SIP scheme launched April 2026 (minimum INR5,000 per month, 10-11 month tenure); about 50 customers contributing above INR1 lakh per month per scheme.
Gold import duty raised from 6% to 15% in May 2026; gold prices corrected in June to about INR1,45,000-1,50,000 per 10 gm from peaks of about INR1,70,000-1,75,000.
Fresh gold procurement at INR1,45,000-1,50,000; weighted-average inventory cost about INR1,20,000, roughly 20% below market, which management said will narrow as new purchases come in.
Inventory mix: about 80% 22-karat, 15% 18-karat, balance lower karat. Management said customers still prefer 22-karat, with lightweight 22-karat designs as the affordability response.
Management said FY26 had no meaningful industry volume growth; competition noted from national brands with multiple stores in Indore.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the DP Swarn Plus scheme and how is it being received?
qa_highlights.answer: Launched April 2026 as a SIP-based gold scheme with a INR5,000 minimum monthly contribution; about 50 customers contribute above INR1 lakh per month per scheme. Revenue contribution was not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FOCO model plan and the FOCO vs COCO mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Jabalpur is a pilot revenue-sharing FOCO store with DP retaining full operational control. Plan is 2-3 franchisee stores a year over the next four to five years, with the 51-store mix described as mostly COCO and a smaller FOCO share.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company reconcile the 51-store target with 3-4 stores added per year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it targets 6 stores in FY26-27 and 6-8 per year from FY28 to FY30; it acknowledged FY27 was slowed by the May developments and said the pace is now back to aggressive expansion.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company hedge gold and silver as it expands?
qa_highlights.answer: Uses real-time replenishment (3-4 bookings a day with vendors), exchange-based old gold purchases, gold metal loans for extra inventory, and MCX hedging.

qa_highlights.question: What is the volume growth and what is the gold-price effect on sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY27 volume grew about 1-2% YoY; the balance of revenue growth came from higher gold prices and making charges. Inventory gains were about 10-15% of growth. Management said volume was not growing meaningfully in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Why does operating cash flow stay negative and how will it improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 95-98% of assets are inventory, so operating cash flow is linked to inventory build. It expects working capital efficiency to improve as the business scales.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inventory carrying value versus market price, and how is it accounted for?
qa_highlights.answer: Weighted-average cost is about INR1,20,000 vs market of INR1,51,000-1,52,000 per gram (a gap of about 20%); the gap will narrow as fresh purchases at INR1,45,000-1,50,000 enter inventory. Management said profitability depends on making charges.

qa_highlights.question: What volume and revenue growth should be expected for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets about 10% volume growth for both FY27 and FY28; revenue growth will depend on gold prices.

risks_watch: Volume growth of only 1-2% against 58% revenue growth; the gap depends on gold prices and making charges.
Operating cash flow has been negative for three years, per an analyst; management attributes it to inventory build.
Gold import duty hike to 15% (May 2026) and gold price volatility affect demand and expansion pace.
Inventory is carried at about 20% below market; gross margin depends on making charges and product mix.
Store rollout risk: 51-store FY30 target needs about 6-8 openings a year, while FY27 has only 5-6 planned; new stores ramp slowly.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand recovery and the 10% volume target, but defensive when pressed on volume growth, cash flow and inventory valuation. Some answers were indirect, and the store mix and karat-level detail were not given cleanly.
key_quotes: Our same -store sales growth stood at 52% on an overa ll basis.
Broadly, we are targeting around 10% volume growth going forward.
Our business currently operates with an inventory turnover ratio of around 4.7x to 5.0x annually , which, in our view, is among the best in the industry.
So, what idea we have taken is that for FY26, FY27, on an overall basis we are looking for six stores whereby one or at the end second franchisee may come in this year.

growth.why: Management targets ~10% volume growth for FY27 and FY28 (internal planning target) backed by 5-6 new stores in FY27 and two showrooms (Jabalpur, Dahod) in fit-out, but Q1 volume grew only 1-2% and the revenue jump was mostly gold price and making charges, so the volume target is not yet demonstrated.
